modelAnswer:
Noah’s aching hands seemed to agree with his brother’s words. He looked down the dark driveway, and for a moment he almost dropped his own shovel too. Then he felt the folded bill in his pocket. Mrs. Williams had paid them before they had moved any snow. “She trusted us, Lucas,” he said quietly. “If we leave now, we’re taking her money for nothing.” Lucas kicked at the snow and said nothing. Noah picked up his brother’s shovel and held it out. After a long moment, Lucas took it. Side by side, slower now, they cleared one narrow strip at a time until only a thin line of snow remained near the street.

As they cleared the final shovel of snow, Mrs. Williams’ car returned. Her headlights swept across the clean driveway, and she stepped out, surprised. “I thought you two would be long gone in this cold,” she said. Lucas lowered his eyes. “We almost were,” he admitted. “But you’d already paid us.” Mrs. Williams looked at their red, numb hands and smiled. “Then I know who to call next time it snows.” On the way home, the brothers stopped at Mr. Henderson’s window. The red bicycle was still far beyond their reach, but with twenty-seven dollars and more work ahead, it no longer seemed impossible.
